newsitem.title: USA: Advanced Tissue confident on DermaGraft.
newsitem.headline: Advanced Tissue confident on DermaGraft.

text.p: Advanced Tissue Sciences Inc said it remained confident its DermaGraft treatment for diabetic foot ulcers would be approved, despite rumors to the contrary that sent the company's share price down sharply.

The rumors started when Morgan Stanley analyst Eric Hecht downgraded the company to a neutral from a strong buy. While Hecht was not immediately available to explain the reason for the downgrade, rumors in the market said he had seen the data on DermaGraft and was unimpressed. Advanced Tissue, however, denied having made the data available.
Advanced Tissue shares were down four to 10-5/8.
According to an Advanced Tissue spokeswoman, the Morgan Stanley downgrade came after the company declined to make its clinical data available to the analyst ahead of schedule.
"We are due to file for premarket approval with the FDA by December 19 and we will not make our data available before then," said spokeswoman, Claudia Flint.
"The company feels very confident in the data," Flint added. "The FDA has already granted us an expedited review of the product."

DermaGraft is a treatment to heal diabetic foot ulcers by inserting living tissue into a patient's wounds. Foot ulcers are common among diabetics, whose poor circulation causes the skin tissue to break down.
